content: Diazolidinyl urea, with the chemical formula C8H14N4O7, functions as a preservative. It is widely utilized due to its broad-spectrum antimicrobial properties, effectively inhibiting the growth of bacteria, fungi, and yeasts. This compound is incorporated into a variety of products, including cosmetics, skin care formulations, shampoos, and conditioners. Additionally, it is present in other consumer goods such as bubble baths, baby wipes, and household cleaning detergents. Diazolidinyl urea is also a key component in the commercially available preservative known as Germaben. However, it is important to note that some individuals may develop a contact allergy to diazolidinyl urea, which can result in dermatitis. Individuals who exhibit sensitivity to diazolidinyl urea are often found to be allergic to imidazolidinyl urea as well.
